appName.description: Extension name shown in the browser.

appDescription.message: FitShield browser extension that helps you stay mindful of food delivery and fast-food ordering.
appDescription.description: Extension description shown in the browser.

timerDurationHint.message: Adjust the countdown before Continue appears.

siteOpenTimeHint.message: Choose how long sites stay open after the timer ends.

scheduleDefaultSummary.message: Blocking will follow your daily schedule when this is enabled.

currentScheduleSummary.description: $1 is a time range, optionally followed by ' every day'.

popupBlockerSubtitle.message: Turn every blocklist on or off.

popupMetadataSubtitle.message: Block whole groups of sites by country or food category.

popupCustomSubtitle.message: Add your own sites and disable them individually.

popupScheduleSubtitle.message: Useful for meal budgets, late-night ordering, or work hours.

statusInactive.message: FitShield is off. Nothing is being blocked.
statusInactive.description: Shown when the master switch is off. The subject is always "FitShield".

statusAllDisabled.message: FitShield is on, but every individual site is switched off. Open Settings to turn some back on.
statusAllDisabled.description: Shown when FitShield is on but every individual site has been switched off.

statusBypassActive.message: Temporary pass is active. Blocking resumes in $1.
statusBypassActive.description: $1 is a remaining-time string such as '4m 12s'.

statusPassSite.message: $1 is open for $2. Everything else is still blocked.
statusPassSite.description: $1 is the site the pass covers, $2 the time remaining. Used when exactly one site has a pass, so the global "blocking resumes" sentence would be false.

statusPassSitesNamed.message: $1 are open for up to $2. Everything else is still blocked.
statusPassSitesNamed.description: $1 is the list of sites that have a pass, already joined by popup.js ("doordash.com, ubereats.com"); $2 is the time until the last pass ends. Used for two or three sites, where naming them still fits the status line. Do not turn $1 back into a count — knowing WHICH sites are open is the point of the sentence.

statusPassSites.message: $1 sites are open for up to $2. Everything else is still blocked.
statusPassSites.description: $1 is how many sites have a pass, $2 the time until the last one ends. Used from four sites upwards, where the list is too long to name and the count is the readable fact.

statusOutsideSchedule.message: FitShield is on, but this is outside your scheduled hours. It will block from $1.
statusOutsideSchedule.description: $1 is a time range. The subject is always "FitShield".

statusShieldUp.message: FitShield is on. $1-second pause, then the site stays open for $2 $3.
statusShieldUp.description: $1 pause length in seconds, $2 how long the site stays open, $3 the localized minute/minutes unit for $2. Same wording as frictionSummary. The subject is always "FitShield" — never "the blocker", "the shield" or "armed".

searchMatchSuffix.description: $1 is the count of matching sites; appended to a count line. Plural verb agreement — searchMatchSuffixOne covers exactly 1.

searchMatchSuffixOne.description: Singular form of searchMatchSuffix, for exactly one match. English needs the -s here; "1 match the search" was ungrammatical.

warningIntro.message: Hunger, habit, stress, and convenience all feel the same in the moment. Here is one thing you could make instead.

warningErrorHint.message: Something went wrong while opening the site. Please try again.

warningStaleHint.message: This page is out of date. Opening the site again so FitShield can interrupt it properly.
warningStaleHint.description: Shown when a block page left open across a browser restart is holding a redirect token the worker no longer recognises. The page then asks for the site again, which produces a fresh block page.

blockReasonAppCategory.message: $1 apps are blocked while app blocking is on.
blockReasonAppCategory.description: Android block screen: why this app was interrupted. $1 is the localized category name (the same catLabel the extension block page and Settings use).

blockReasonMoreCountries.description: $1 is the number of additional countries not shown.

customizeBlocklistIntro.message: Choose which built-in groups are active, turn individual sites on or off, and add your own domains.

customUrlsSettingsSubtitle.message: Add your own domains and disable them individually.

allBlocklistsHint.message: Turn every built-in group on or off at once.

customNormalizeHint.message: Entries are normalized to domains and blocked across all pages.

customEmptyDefault.message: No custom blocked sites yet. Add a domain like example.com above to start blocking it.

customNoMatch.message: No custom URLs match this search.

emptyDeliverySearch.message: No delivery sites match this search.

emptyFastFoodSearch.message: No fast food sites match this search.

noticeMatched.description: $1 count, $2 site/sites unit, $3 the search term.

invalidUrlNotice.message: That URL does not look valid yet. Try a domain like example.com.

alreadyOnBlocklist.message: $1 is already on the blocklist, so it has been re-enabled.

addedToBlocklist.message: $1 was added to the custom blocklist.

removedFromBlocklist.message: $1 was removed from the custom blocklist.

metadataIntro.message: Block whole groups of sites by the country a brand operates in or the kind of food it serves. These blocks add to your existing site and custom-URL blocks.

blockByCountryHint.message: Search by country name or code, e.g. "United" or "US". Enabling a country blocks every brand active there.

countryQuickEmpty.message: Enable a country from search to pin it here.

blockByCategoryHint.message: Search categories like burger, pizza, or coffee. Specialties are searchable too; the block applies by category.

categoryQuickEmpty.message: Enable a category from search to pin it here.

languageIntro.message: Choose the language FitShield uses for its own screens. This overrides your browser language for the extension only.

languageHint.message: Search for a language and select it. Choose System default to follow your browser.

mbBlocking.description: State of a country/category in the search results: it IS being blocked. Pairs with mbBlock.

mbBlock.description: State of a country/category in the search results: it is NOT being blocked. Pairs with mbBlocking.

mbChipRemoveAria.description: $1 is a country or category label.

systemThemeHint.message: Device preference or a fixed mode.

backupIntro.message: Save your FitShield settings to a file, or restore them on another device. Everything stays on your device — nothing is uploaded.

exportErrorNotice.message: FitShield could not save the backup file. Check that downloads are allowed for this browser, then try again.
exportErrorNotice.description: Shown when WRITING a backup fails. Nothing the user chose was at fault and no file exists yet, so this must not blame the file.

importSuccessNotice.description: $1 is the number of settings restored.

importCancelledNotice.description: Shown when the user declines the import confirmation. Must make clear that no settings were touched.

confirmImportBackup.message: Restore $1 settings from this file? They replace what is on this profile, and any active temporary pass and unanswered "did you make it?" prompt are cleared. This cannot be undone.
confirmImportBackup.description: $1 is the number of settings in the file. Confirmation before a destructive import; it must keep naming the two things that are also cleared.

importErrorNotice.message: That file isn't a valid FitShield backup.
importErrorNotice.description: Last-resort import failure text. The backupError* strings below are preferred whenever the reason is known.

backupErrorNotBackup.message: That file is not a FitShield backup.
backupErrorNotBackup.description: Import failure: the file parsed, but it is not a FitShield backup at all.

backupErrorNewerFormat.message: That backup was written by a newer version of FitShield (format $1). Update FitShield, then import it.
backupErrorNewerFormat.description: $1 is the backup's format number. The file IS valid — do not translate this as if the backup were broken, or the user may delete their only copy.

backupErrorNoSettings.message: That backup contains no FitShield settings.
backupErrorNoSettings.description: Import failure: the file is a backup in shape but carries none of the settings FitShield restores.

backupErrorEmptyFile.description: Import failure: the chosen file has no contents.

backupErrorTooLarge.message: That file is too large to be a FitShield backup ($1 KB; the limit is $2 KB).
backupErrorTooLarge.description: $1 is the file's size in KB, $2 the limit in KB. KB is the unit symbol.

backupErrorInvalidJson.description: Import failure: the file could not be parsed. JSON is a format name and stays untranslated.

backupErrorValidatorMissing.message: FitShield could not validate that backup. Reload the page and try again.
backupErrorValidatorMissing.description: Import failure inside FitShield rather than in the file: the shared validator was not available, so the import stopped instead of restoring unchecked settings.

reorderCardLabel.message: Reorder card: $1. Use arrow keys to move it.
reorderCardLabel.description: $1 is the card's title. Accessible label for the drag handle.

statsIntro.message: Counts of things that actually happened, kept on this device. Every number is one observed event — nothing here is inferred, and nothing is uploaded.

estimatesToggleHint.message: Off by default. It multiplies the alternatives you marked as made by a price you choose. That is an assumption, not a measurement — FitShield cannot see what you ordered or spent.

estimateBasis.message: $1 alternatives you marked as made, at $2 each.
estimateBasis.description: $1 is the count (always 2 or more), $2 the price. estimateBasisOne covers exactly 1.

estimateBasisOne.message: 1 alternative you marked as made, at $1 each.
estimateBasisOne.description: Singular form of estimateBasis, for exactly one alternative. $1 is the price; the count is written out, so this takes ONE placeholder where the plural takes two.

currencyLabel.description: Accessible name for the currency picker beside the meal-cost field. The two controls previously shared one label, so a screen reader announced both as "Average meal cost".

currencyAuto.description: The first entry in the currency picker: follow the display language instead of pinning a currency. $1 is the currency name, $2 its symbol. A globe emoji was previously the only thing distinguishing this from the real currency of the same name, and screen readers drop it.

avgMealCostBasisHint.message: What one delivery order usually costs you. Stored on your device only.

resetIntro.message: Restore parts of FitShield to their defaults. Each action asks for confirmation first.

resetBlockingHint.message: Timers, schedule, site toggles, custom URLs, and country/category blocks.

resetStatsHint.message: Your counters, the most-blocked lists, your favorites, and the estimate settings.

factoryResetHint.message: Erase everything and return FitShield to a fresh install.

confirmResetBlocking.message: Reset all blocking settings to their defaults? Your theme, language, and saved stats are kept.

confirmResetAppearance.message: Reset the theme and appearance to the default dark mode?

confirmResetStats.message: Reset every statistic, your favorites, and the estimate settings? Your blocklist, schedule, kitchen, and the alternatives you wrote yourself are kept.

confirmFactoryReset.message: Factory reset FitShield? This erases all settings, custom sites, and stats on this device. This cannot be undone.

welcomeSubtitle.message: A few quick choices and you're set. Everything stays on your device — nothing is uploaded.

welcomeLangBody.message: This sets the language for FitShield's popup, settings, and block screen.

welcomeThemeBody.message: You can fine-tune colors later in Settings.

welcomeDeliveryBody.message: A short pause screen replaces the ordering page, with something you could make instead.
welcomeDeliveryBody.description: Body text under the onboarding question 'What should FitShield interrupt?'. Covers every answer (delivery and fast food), so it must not name one kind of site.

welcomeImportBody.message: Coming from another device? Import a FitShield settings file to bring everything over. Otherwise just continue.

welcomeStepLabel.description: $1 is the current step number, $2 is the total.

whatsNewSubtitle.message: A quick look at what changed.

supportFooterText.message: If FitShield helped you avoid an unnecessary delivery order, optional support helps keep blocklists and docs moving.

timerDoneAnnounce.message: The pause is over. You can continue if you choose to.

warningSentenceEnd.description: The full stop that ends the "You opened <brand>" sentence on the block page. It is a separate key because the brand name is emphasised, so the sentence cannot be one message with a placeholder. Latin-script locales keep "."; zh/ja/yue use the ideographic full stop, which is what the rest of their corpus uses.

warningLockedHint.message: Continuing unlocks when the pause ends.

warningUnlockedHint.message: You can continue whenever you want to.

repeatFrictionNote.message: You continued to this site recently, so this pause is $1 seconds longer. It goes back to normal after $2 minutes, and you can switch this off in settings.

previewBanner.message: Preview. This is what a real interruption looks like. Nothing here is recorded and no site is blocked.

previewPassNote.message: In a real interruption this would open the site. Nothing was changed.

intentSubtitle.message: Optional. This only shapes what you are shown right now — it is not saved.

intentLegitimate.message: I need to place a real order

intentBrowsingAnnounce.message: Alternatives hidden. Go back is the first action.

alternativeChooseButton.description: Selects an alternative on the block page. It must not use "make": "made" names only the event the user later confirms in the popup.

alternativeChosenNote.message: Noted as your plan. FitShield has not recorded a meal — you can confirm you made it from the popup later, if you want to.

noAlternativeFound.message: No alternative matched. Try clearing a filter.

relaxedEquipment.message: No exact match for your equipment — closest option shown

relaxedTime.message: Nothing matched that time limit — closest option shown

relaxedFastest.message: No fast option matched — closest option shown

relaxedNoCook.message: No no-cook option matched — closest option shown

relaxedMicrowave.message: No microwave-only option matched — closest option shown

passTitle.message: How do you want to continue?
passTitle.description: Heading of the block page's continue panel. Scope-neutral: the panel offers site-scoped AND all-scope options.

passSubtitle.message: Choose how long. Each option says what it covers — this site only, or all blocking.
passSubtitle.description: Sits above six buttons, four scoped to this site and two that turn all blocking off. It must not promise that FitShield stays on, because two of the buttons switch it off.

passConfiguredMinutes.description: $1 is the user’s own Site open time setting.

passAllThirtyMinutes.message: Turn off all blocking for 30 minutes
passAllThirtyMinutes.description: Turns ALL blocking off, not just this site. "Pause" is reserved for the block-page countdown.

passAllUntilTomorrow.message: Turn off all blocking until tomorrow
passAllUntilTomorrow.description: Turns ALL blocking off, not just this site. "Pause" is reserved for the block-page countdown.

frictionIntro.message: Pick a starting point. You can change any value afterwards — doing so simply moves you to Custom.

frictionSummary.message: $1-second pause, then the site stays open for $2 minutes.

frictionCustomSummary.message: Custom: $1-second pause, then the site stays open for $2 minutes.

askIntentHint.message: A short, skippable question on the block page. The answer is never saved.

repeatFrictionHint.message: Adds one small, fixed amount of extra pause if you come back to the same site soon after continuing. It never grows beyond that, and the block page always says why.

scheduleIntro.message: Times follow your device clock, so they keep their meaning across daylight-saving changes.

scheduleAlwaysSummary.message: FitShield is on all the time.

scheduleWindowsSummary.description: $1 is the number of windows, always 2 or more. scheduleWindowsSummaryOne covers exactly 1.

scheduleWindowsSummaryOne.description: Singular form of scheduleWindowsSummary, for exactly one window.

scheduleOvernightHint.message: A window whose end time is earlier than its start crosses midnight, and belongs to the day it starts on.

kitchenIntro.message: Optional. This only changes the order alternatives are suggested in — nothing is ever hidden from you, and no quantities, dates, or shopping history are stored.

dietHint.message: A stricter diet is a hard filter: you will never be shown something that breaks it.

allergenHint.message: Also a hard filter. FitShield uses the declared allergens in its own catalog and cannot check what you cook.

customAltIntro.message: Add the things you actually make. They appear alongside the built-in suggestions, stay on this device, and are included in your backup.

customAltEmpty.message: You have not added any yet.

recapHeading.description: Heading of the rolling seven-day summary. The same window is called "Last 7 days" in the popup.

recapNoActivity.message: Nothing to summarize for the last 7 days.
recapNoActivity.description: Rolling seven days, not a calendar week — the wording must not imply a Monday reset.

previewIntro.message: Open a simulated interruption so you can see the block page, the countdown, an alternative, and the pass options.

previewRecordsNothing.message: In preview nothing is recorded: no interruption is counted, no alternative is added to your history, no pass is granted, and no site is unblocked.

reportIntro.message: FitShield never sends anything on its own. Fill this in, see exactly what it would say, then copy it or open a pre-filled message yourself.

reportCopied.message: Copied. Nothing has been sent — paste it wherever you want to.

reportCopyFailed.message: Could not reach the clipboard. The report is shown above; select and copy it.

reportPrivacyNote.message: Query strings are stripped and only the domain is included. Your browsing history, page contents, settings, and statistics are never part of a report.

reportMissingSite.message: A site that should be interrupted is not

reportFalsePositive.message: A site is interrupted that should not be

reportWrongCategory.message: A site is in the wrong category

reportWrongDiet.message: An alternative has the wrong diet label

reportWrongAllergen.message: An alternative has the wrong allergen label

reportBadInstructions.message: The instructions are unclear or wrong

reportSuggestAlternative.message: I want to suggest an alternative

onboardingFrictionQuestion.message: How much friction do you want?

onboardingPreviewBody.message: When you open one of those sites, FitShield replaces the page with a short pause and one thing you could make instead. You can always go back, or continue on purpose.

onboardingAdvancedNote.message: Everything else — countries, categories, individual sites, your kitchen, and your own alternatives — is in settings whenever you want it.

diagTitle.description: Diagnostics page. Title bar and main heading. 'FitShield' is the product name and stays as-is.

diagSubtitle.message: Live view of the extension runtime. If blocking isn't working, the answer is here.

diagRuntimeHeading.description: Section heading: what the extension itself is doing right now.

diagManifestLabel.description: Row label. The value beside it is the extension name and version.

diagServiceWorkerLabel.description: Row label. The background process that decides what to block.

diagEngineLabel.description: Row label. 'FS Engine' is a component name and stays untranslated.

diagBlockPageUrlLabel.description: Row label. The address of the page shown in place of a blocked site.

diagBrandsLabel.description: Row label. How many brands the blocklist data holds.

diagBucketsLabel.description: Row label. The value is two counts separated by a slash, in this order.

diagRulesLabel.description: Row label. Chrome-only; 'Chrome' is a browser name and stays untranslated.

diagTestHeading.description: Section heading for the check-one-domain tool.

diagDomainLabel.description: Accessible name for the domain input. It is a name, not an instruction.

diagDomainPlaceholder.description: Placeholder text. The domain is an example and must stay exactly as written; translate only the 'e.g.' abbreviation.

diagCheckButton.description: Button that runs the typed domain through the engine.

diagTestNote.message: Runs the domain through the engine — no navigation, nothing stored.
diagTestNote.description: Reassurance under the domain test: checking a domain neither opens it nor records it.

diagRefreshButton.description: Button that re-reads every value on the diagnostics page.

diagValueResponding.description: Service worker row value: the background service answered.

diagValueNotResponding.description: Service worker row value: the background service did not answer.

diagValueLoaded.description: FS Engine row value: the blocking engine is in memory.

diagValueMissing.description: FS Engine row value: the blocking engine did not load.

diagValueNone.description: Last error row value: there is no recorded error.

diagValueError.description: Row value when reading a figure failed. $1 is the underlying message.

diagOpenBlockPage.description: Link beside the block page address. It previously read "open warning.html", exposing a source filename.

diagWorkerDown.message: FitShield's background service is not responding, so nothing is being blocked.
diagWorkerDown.description: Banner shown when the diagnostics page gets no answer at all.

diagAllGood.message: FitShield is installed and running. The rows below show what it is doing right now.
diagAllGood.description: Diagnostics banner when every check passed. Stated rather than implied by silence, because an empty banner reads as "nothing was checked".

diagWorkerDownFix.message: Turn FitShield off and back on from your browser's extensions page. If that does not help, restart your browser.
diagWorkerDownFix.description: What a customer can actually do about it. This replaced an instruction to run a Node build script and load an unpacked folder, which no store customer can follow.

diagEngineDown.message: Part of FitShield did not load, so nothing will be blocked.
diagEngineDown.description: Banner shown when the FS Engine bundle is missing.

diagDetails.description: Prefix for the raw error text under a banner. $1 is not translated — it is whatever the browser reported.

diagChecking.description: Shown while a typed domain is being tested.

diagNoResult.description: The domain test returned nothing to report.

diagTestBlocked.message: “$1” would be interrupted — FitShield would show the block page instead.
diagTestBlocked.description: $1 is the domain that was tested. "Interrupted" is the product's word for a blocked page load.

diagTestOpen.message: “$1” is not on the blocklist — it would open normally.
diagTestOpen.description: $1 is the domain that was tested.

diagCheckFailed.description: $1 is the domain that was typed, $2 the reason it could not be checked.

diagTestNoAnswer.message: FitShield's background service did not respond: $1
